chunks.text: Machine learning models require careful validation to ensure they generalize well to unseen data. Cross-validation techniques split the dataset into training and testing sets, allowing practitioners to assess model performance objectively. This approach helps identify overfitting and guides hyperparameter tuning for optimal results.

chunks.text: Data quality validation in RAG systems prevents indexing corrupted PDFs, duplicate content, and boilerplate-heavy text. chunks.text: Neural networks consist of interconnected layers of artificial neurons that process information through weighted connections. The backpropagation algorithm adjusts these weights during training by calculating gradients of the loss function. Deep learning architectures stack multiple layers to learn hierarchical representations, enabling breakthrough performance in computer vision and natural language processing tasks.

chunks.text: Vector databases enable efficient similarity search for RAG applications by storing embeddings in high-dimensional spaces. Approximate nearest neighbor algorithms like HNSW and IVF provide sub-linear query times, making them suitable for production systems with millions of documents. Proper index tuning balances recall accuracy against latency requirements.
